text:
The **Studienstiftung** is a prestigious German scholarship program founded in 1925, initially as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft. After being dissolved under National Socialism, it was reestablished in 1948 as a registered association in Cologne. The program offers scholarships to exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates based on criteria similar to those of the German state support system (BAföG). It supports full-time university studies in Germany, the EU, or Switzerland, with no citizenship or age restrictions.
Admission is open to students nominated by schools, professors, examination boards, national or international competitions, or self-nomination through an assessment test. Scholars receive financial support (monthly allowance, need-based scholarships, health insurance) and academic benefits, including summer schools, mentoring, and research opportunities. The program also supports doctoral candidates and offers specialized scholarships in cooperation with other institutions.
As of 2023, the Studienstiftung provides scholarships to over 14,888 students annually, with a notable gender balance (55.4% women). It has supported influential figures across science, social sciences, business, politics, arts, and journalism, including Nobel Prize winners and prominent public figures. The program emphasizes excellence, initiative, and responsibility, fostering a network of scholars committed to societal contributions.
